SPARKS 2.0 is a grant programme run by PI-RAHI, the Panjab University and IIT Ropar regional accelerator that sits under the Northern Region S&T Cluster of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser. It is aimed at research-driven startups that already have a working MVP with technology at TRL 4 or above.

Selected startups can receive grant support of up to ₹10 lakh, along with mentorship from the PU–IIT Ropar ecosystem, help with IP protection and commercialisation strategy, and introductions to investors and further funding sources.

You should be a Private Limited Company, or be willing to incorporate as one within three months of selection. Your innovation must fit a theme such as agriculture and food processing, green mobility and energy, pharma, medical devices and healthcare, waste-to-wealth, or indigenous technology. Startups from Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir get preference, but founders from elsewhere in India can still apply.

The catch founders miss: PI-RAHI has not published equity terms or a document checklist, so email them if that matters, and keep your TRL evidence and a short technical deck ready before you open the form.

A government will fund your startup with up to ₹69 lakh and take zero equity. The government is Chile's.

Start-Up Chile, the accelerator backed by the Chilean government agency CORFO, is accepting applications for its 13th generation, called BIG 13. Founders from any country and any industry can apply, including Indian teams.

There are three tracks. Build runs for four months and suits teams moving from a validated idea to a first prototype, with about CLP 15 million in co-financed funding. Ignite also runs four months, for startups with an MVP chasing product-market fit, with about CLP 30 million. Growth runs six months for companies scaling and raising capital, with up to CLP 75 million, roughly ₹69 lakh. Every track is equity-free and comes with free co-working in Chile, training, board sessions and access to Start-Up Chile's investor and corporate networks. Teams led by women can get a higher funding share.

The catch: you are expected to run the business from Chile during the programme. Start-Up Chile helps foreign founders get a work visa, but plan for the move, and note that the Build track needs your own co-financing.

Applications close at 1:00 PM Chile time, which is 9:30 PM IST.

Has anyone in the world built your health technology before? If the answer is no, ICMR may fund it with up to ₹8 crore.

The Indian Council of Medical Research has opened its First in the World Challenge Grants 2026. This is a high-risk, high-reward call for vaccines, drugs, diagnostics or interventions that have never been attempted anywhere. Incremental improvements on existing products are rejected outright.

Funding is non-dilutive and released in stages against deliverables: up to ₹1 crore over two years for proof of concept, up to ₹4 crore over three years for a prototype, and up to ₹8 crore over four years for the final product or model.

Indian startups, MSMEs and industry can apply, as can government medical colleges, national institutes, universities and recognised R&D labs. Private institutions and NGOs need DSIR recognition as research organisations. Each proposal needs a Principal Investigator plus at least one Co-PI from the same institution.

The tip founders often miss: submissions are accepted only on ICMR's e-PMS portal, and incomplete proposals are rejected before anyone reviews the science. Register on the portal early and do not leave the upload for the final evening.

Applications close at 5:30 PM IST.
